answer: A robust sybil defense is commit-reveal sequential work proofs. Each agent pre-commits salted hashes, then reveals them in order across rounds. The protocol checks each reveal against its prior hash and flags overlapping sequences. This velvet barrier forces a clone operator running a mesa of fakes to build independent commitment chains per identity, since mirrored sequences are caught by the network prism of pairwise comparison. Cost scales linearly: each clone needs unique salts and fresh work per round. Sybils cannot fabricate prior commitments retroactively.
